overview: Memeware 7.3's LongJump is a dormant skeleton: both registered event handlers are empty lambdas, so the module has zero observable effect on the packet stream, and its three fields (currentMotion, previousDistance, currentPhase) plus the registered modes ('NCP', 'Mineplex', 'Hypixel') are the only trace of the longjump algorithm it was meant to run. The field names map onto the classic NCP-style longjump state machine: a currentPhase that steps through the sub-0.42 jump offsets, a previousDistance fed by each tick's horizontal displacement, and a currentMotion that decays as lastDist minus lastDist over 159.998 after a grounded reset to 0.2873 times 2.15. None of that logic exists in the file; the module compiles, registers its modes, and sends nothing.

sections.p: The file is 30 lines: three double fields, a constructor that registers the 'NCP', 'Mineplex' and 'Hypixel' modes, and two lwjeb-registered consumers. The UpdateEvent consumer (eventConsumer0) is an empty lambda; the MovementEvent consumer (eventConsumer1) is also an empty lambda. There is no onEnable, onDisable, timer, or packet send anywhere in the file. The event infrastructure fires both handlers on schedule, and neither mutates anything, so enabling the module changes the client's behavior not at all. The declared fields are never read, which the compiler does not flag because they are instance state.

The field names document the intended algorithm precisely. currentPhase is the jump-phase counter of the classic NCP longjump: on the grounded tick the module would apply the 0.424-ish jump velocity and step the phase, then re-apply it on the following ticks until the phase limit. previousDistance would be assigned from Math.hypot(x, z) of the per-tick delta, and currentMotion would follow the decay model: a grounded reset to 0.2873 * 2.15 (the vanilla base speed times the longjump multiplier), an air increment of 0.15 times the excess over base on the first air tick, and then the geometric decay lastDist - lastDist / 159.998 that keeps the horizontal speed just under what the old NCP model predicted per tick. The Mineplex and Hypixel registrations imply the usual per-server variants of the same decay loop with different strafe multipliers and timer adjustments, but no branch for any of them exists.

Because both handlers are empty, the module never sends a C03 of its own, never edits the movement event, and never touches the timer or the onGround flag. The packet stream while the module is enabled is byte-identical to the stream while it is disabled: vanilla movement packets at the normal rate. The practical consequence is that the module is a placeholder: activating it provides no speed, and none of the countering checks in this analysis can ever observe it, because there is nothing to observe. The analysis of the dormant pattern below still matters, because the fields and mode list are a precise spec for what the module does the moment a handler is wired.

files.label: LongJump.java (module)
files.explanation: This 30-line file is the entire module. The constructor registers the NCP, Mineplex and Hypixel modes and the module name; the two handlers (eventConsumer0 on UpdateEvent, eventConsumer1 on MovementEvent) are empty lambdas; the three fields currentMotion, previousDistance and currentPhase are the dormant state of the classic NCP longjump decay loop and are never read. There is no other logic, no packet send, and no timer manipulation. The file exists as a skeleton whose handlers were left unwired.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (horizontal speed envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly's horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation, which predicts the per-tick sprint distance (0.91 air inertia, sprint +30%) and measures the reported move against it; the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back. The dormant fields encode the classic NCP longjump that this envelope is the modern form of: the 0.2873 * 2.15 grounded reset produces a 0.6177 blocks-per-tick move against a predicted ~0.31, so hDistanceAboveLimit is around 0.31 and the violation is about 31 on the first grounded tick; the 159.998 decay model keeps the air speed above the prediction for the whole arc, so the accumulated violations climb each tick. The 0.42-stage vertical phases are the one part the envelope tolerates: isJumpMotion grants a jumpDelay window of 10 ticks, so the jump itself passes; the horizontal pin is what fails. As shipped the module never fires, so the check sees only vanilla traffic and never flags.

countering.label: Speed (stage table and ground expectation)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Speed check models expected horizontal speed per air stage: 0.049 added when vertical is zero, 0.08 when descending under 0.34, 0.3261 when rising at or above 0.34, all on top of a base of 0.2873 (scaled by speed potions), and on the ground an expected of thisMove divided by groundTime plus baseMove once groundTicks reaches 5. The dormant decay loop is exactly the profile this table rejects: after the grounded reset the first air tick moves at 0.6177 against a rising-stage expectation of 0.6134, which barely passes, but every descending tick at the same magnitude runs against 0.3673 and flags with the BunnyHop label, and the grounded re-reset at 0.6177 against 0.3498 flags once groundTicks hits 5. The module would survive only the first rising tick of each jump, then violate on descent. As shipped, nothing fires and the check stays silent.

countering.label: Speed (momentum conservation)
countering.explanation: Hawk's Speed check conserves momentum: expected speed is friction times the previous speed plus a small set of adders (the vanilla sprint-jump +0.2, hit slowdown, block slipperiness), and the discrepancy between the reported speed and the expectation accumulates per player until it crosses the 0.1 threshold, then punishAndTryRubberband with the VL scaled by the discrepancy. The dormant pattern's grounded reset to 0.6177 from a friction-decayed previous speed of about 0.2 yields a discrepancy near 0.4 on the very first move after reset, several times the threshold, and the air decay keeps the magnitude above the momentum model for the whole arc. The jump adder forgives only the vanilla 0.2 sprint-jump boost, not a magnitude pinned to 2.15 times base. As shipped, the module sends nothing, so Hawk's model sees vanilla movement and the accumulated discrepancy stays at zero.
